name: Meera notes (SYNTHETIC SAMPLE - not real notes)

messages.text: reading a paper at 11pm on preservative efficacy testing. challenge test = you deliberately contaminate the product and see if the preservative kills it off in 28 days. most customers have no idea this exists. the 'preservative-free' crowd would hate how necessary it is
remind self: order more airless pumps before sept

at the unit today. batch had a slight colour shift in the last third of the run. CoA from start of run was fine. this is EXACTLY why we insisted on mid-batch sampling. supplier asked why we care if it's 'within spec'. because within spec at the start isn't within spec at the end
customer DM: 'your serum isn't working, I've used it 5 days.' Nothing works in 5 days. skin cell turnover is roughly 4 weeks. how do I say this without sounding defensive

text: another DM asking if our serum is 'preservative free'. no. water-based products without a preservative system are a contamination risk within weeks of opening.

text.text: preservative-free is not a safety claim

text: . it's a marketing claim that moves the risk to the customer

messages.text: influencer sent us a 'collab' brief. wanted us to say the serum 'transforms skin in 7 days'. said no.
monsoon returns data: texture complaints up again in Kochi but only on the moisturiser, not the serum. we never reformulated the moisturiser base. same mistake twice?

thought: people ask 'how long until I see results' and the honest answer depends on what result. hydration = days. pigmentation = 8-12 weeks. nobody puts timelines on labels because the honest ones are long
saw a brand launch a 'waterless' serum as if water is the enemy. waterless mostly means you need less preservative. that's a real formulation benefit but they're selling it as purity
